9NS86BQ33SPX:couch.text: A cheerful open-world sandbox where you take silly jobs, do mini games and wander a colourful town together on split-screen. The exploring and low-pressure goofing around echo LEGO games and Stardew's earn-and-spend loop.
9NS86BQ33SPX:couch.caveat: It's more of a loose sandbox than a guided story, so it may feel aimless without the puzzle and mystery structure they like.

9NXVC0482QS5:couch.text: A two-player split-screen adventure where each level hands you different abilities and puzzles to solve together, with a funny, heartfelt story. It's close to A Way Out in format and the cute, inventive tone of their favourites.
9NXVC0482QS5:couch.caveat: Some platforming and boss sections demand quick timing, which could frustrate Tay if skill gaps show.

C4VKLMG1HLZW:couch.text: Two yarn creatures swing, climb and pull each other through gentle platforming puzzles in pretty, colourful landscapes. The cooperation is the core, which suits a shared-screen pair who enjoy It Takes Two.
C4VKLMG1HLZW:couch.caveat: Some stages need precise jumping and timing, and the co-op can get fiddly when one player lags behind.

C042M8GWKS34:couch.text: You hop into larger and smaller nesting dolls and use each one's special ability to solve quirky puzzles with a humorous, storybook feel. Puzzles can be tackled in different ways, so there's little pressure.
C042M8GWKS34:couch.caveat: The co-op listing is flagged as conflicting, so confirm two-player local play really works before committing.

9NMB4T25W817:couch.text: A goofy open-world sandbox where you wreck things as a goat, explore, and try silly challenges together on split-screen. It leans on the same exploring and joking around as the LEGO games.
9NMB4T25W817:couch.caveat: There's no real puzzle or story structure, so the novelty may wear off sooner than their favourites.

BSMZH25V6V46:couch.text: Two wobbly characters work out physical puzzles in dreamlike levels, pushing, carrying and climbing to reach the exit. It has the figure-it-out feel of Escape Academy with a slapstick tone.
BSMZH25V6V46:couch.caveat: The floaty controls and climbing can be awkward and frustrating, especially for someone who dislikes fiddly handling.

9PC4RWP34M2D:couch.text: You place wobbly units on a battlefield and watch them fight in a physics-driven comedy. The humour is the draw, and the split-screen mode is versus rather than co-op.
9PC4RWP34M2D:couch.caveat: The local mode is head-to-head, not co-op, and it's a strategy sim with little puzzle or adventure.

9P88K6NQW12H:couch.text: You and Tay haul furniture and awkward items through houses and odd levels, coordinating throws and carries. It's silly, colourful and has an easygoing teamwork feel similar to the LEGO games.
9P88K6NQW12H:couch.caveat: Later levels can get chaotic and time-pressured, which may stress Tay.

9NZG72SH3H4W:couch.text: You load up vehicles and deliver parcels around a wobbly open world, with physics making every trip a joke. Exploring and goofing around together fits the light LEGO-style mood.
9NZG72SH3H4W:couch.caveat: Controls are deliberately floppy and reviews are middling, so it may feel clumsy rather than charming.

9P743P6195Q5:couch.text: A sequel to a game they already like: you work through themed escape rooms together on split-screen, with a mystery about the school running underneath. Same puzzle-solving format, in a fresh campus setting.
9P743P6195Q5:couch.caveat: Some rooms are timed, and tough puzzles could leave one of you stuck, though it's co-op so you can talk it through.

9NR7XDNVP5SW:couch.text: An interactive drama where you make story choices together, with mystery and an emotional, adult storyline. It's close to A Way Out in its story-first approach and needs only simple controls.
9NR7XDNVP5SW:couch.caveat: It has dark themes and tense moments, and it's mostly choosing options rather than puzzles, so it may be heavier than they want.

BQ9Q620NC614:couch.text: A fairy-tale adventure with hand-painted art, where one player guides the heroine and the other controls a small companion. Turn-based battles and light exploration keep it gentle.
BQ9Q620NC614:couch.caveat: The second player has a limited role, and the turn-based RPG combat may feel slow or fiddly for a co-op pair.

9N6Z8DQXSQWH:couch.text: You wander Disneyland together, meeting characters and doing small quests tied to the attractions. It's easygoing and exploratory, which fits the relaxed side of their tastes.
9N6Z8DQXSQWH:couch.caveat: It's aimed at younger kids, so the quests are simple and may feel shallow.

BTBWBGKPKS97:couch.text: A dark-humoured puzzle platformer where a team of adventurers explores a talking cave, each with a special ability. Puzzles need cooperation and the tone is wry rather than frightening.
BTBWBGKPKS97:couch.caveat: It's built for three players, so two will have to handle a character each plus an AI one, and it involves some backtracking.

9PLF73SS7M6J:couch.text: A collection of Rabbids mini-games with some puzzle and adventure elements, all silly and family-friendly. Easy to pick up for a short evening.
9PLF73SS7M6J:couch.caveat: Mini-game compilations tend to be shallow and lack the story and puzzle depth they enjoy.

C26K4DVGR45B:couch.text: A colourful platformer with short levels you run and jump through together, plus music-driven stages. It's lively and funny and fits their couch-platformer taste.
C26K4DVGR45B:couch.caveat: Later levels demand good timing and quick reactions, which may be too high-skill for Tay.

BWVBNCMF22ZK:couch.text: A prison-escape story played entirely as a pair on split-screen, with each player in their own role and some puzzle-ish moments. It's one they already like.
BWVBNCMF22ZK:couch.caveat: They've already played it, so it's a repeat unless they want another run.

9NFQ1XMXDLN6:couch.text: A bright, simple platformer where two players explore themed worlds and do mini-games with Gabby's cats. Very easy to pick up.
9NFQ1XMXDLN6:couch.caveat: It's made for young children, so it may feel too simple and repetitive for two adults.

C3B1V55CDL0C:couch.text: A free platform fighter with plenty of characters, local play for up to eight, and a family-friendly cartoon look. It could work as a casual party game.
C3B1V55CDL0C:couch.caveat: It's competitive fighting that rewards skill and practice, which runs against Tay's dislike of high-skill games.

9NJWFF2KHL6H:couch.text: A 3D platformer in which you explore a cartoon Europe as Ben 10, switching aliens to solve puzzles and fight. Two-player split-screen keeps it LEGO-like.
9NJWFF2KHL6H:couch.caveat: Combat is a big part of it, and review scores are middling.

C2WKJJ9F5936:couch.text: A big fantasy RPG with exploration, quests and a dog companion, and a second player can join locally. It has a lot to see and do.
C2WKJJ9F5936:couch.caveat: The co-op listing is flagged as single, it's combat-driven, and it's long, so it's a weak match for their puzzle-leaning tastes.

9N8NJ74FZTG9:couch.text: A colourful, Minecraft-style dungeon crawler where you fight through levels and collect loot together on one TV. It's easy to pick up and cute.
9N8NJ74FZTG9:couch.caveat: Combat is the whole game and gets hectic, which may not suit Tay.

BVJLKDG2TX8H:couch.text: A frantic cooking game where you chop, cook and pass dishes around quirky kitchens together. It's colourful and rewards communication.
BVJLKDG2TX8H:couch.caveat: Levels are timed and get chaotic, which could cause stress and arguments for a pair who prefer a calm pace.

BR46KM4D5B9L:couch.text: An action RPG with a humorous tone, an open world to explore and a story about leading a kingdom, with a second player able to join.
BR46KM4D5B9L:couch.caveat: Combat-heavy and menu-driven, with less puzzle and mystery than they usually look for.

9N79TQTZTQQ4:couch.text: A pixel-art Marvel beat 'em up with short levels and simple controls, playable by up to four on one TV.
9N79TQTZTQQ4:couch.caveat: It's wall-to-wall fighting with no puzzles or exploration, which cuts against what they enjoy.

9NQVHHW88XW9:couch.text: A gentle, kid-friendly adventure where two players explore Bluey's world and solve simple puzzles together. The low-pressure, cartoonish approach is close to the relaxed puzzle-and-explore pace of Escape Academy and the LEGO games.
9NQVHHW88XW9:couch.caveat: It is clearly aimed at young children, so the puzzles may feel very easy and short for two adults.

BWT2GPVWCH2F:couch.text: Two players share one screen as monarchs, riding a horse across a pixel-art land, collecting coins and building up a small kingdom. The pace is slow and the controls are simple, with a mysterious forest to explore.
BWT2GPVWCH2F:couch.caveat: Nights bring waves of attackers and the game explains little, so it can turn tense and confusing, and the work is more about managing resources than solving puzzles.

BX27S00SKW1V:couch.text: A funny, colourful 3D platformer full of collecting and exploring, in the same spirit as the LEGO games. The split-screen mode is the catch for your profile.
BX27S00SKW1V:couch.caveat: The two-player part is versus minigames, not co-op through the adventure. The main game is single-player, and its camera and platforming can be fiddly.

BQRB60PW2SDL:couch.text: A cartoon kart racer with split-screen for up to four. You race wacky tracks, grab power-ups and fire weapons at each other. It is silly and colourful, with a familiar arcade feel.
BQRB60PW2SDL:couch.caveat: It is competitive racing, not co-op puzzling, and the AI can be tough, with drifting and boosting that takes some skill, so the harder races could frustrate Tay.

9P8XKV2D5DZ5:couch.text: You dig underground for resources, then hurry back to defend your dome from alien waves, and split-screen lets two people share the job. There is a nice exploration and upgrade loop, and it suits a team of two.
9P8XKV2D5DZ5:couch.caveat: The timed waves and dark atmosphere add pressure, and the roguelike runs can be hard, which may stress Tay.

C3553MB4P5TT:couch.text: An isometric action-adventure where two or more players solve environmental puzzles and work together to get through Egyptian temples. Teaming up on switches and traps is similar to the puzzle side of the LEGO games.
C3553MB4P5TT:couch.caveat: Much of the game is shooting enemy hordes and dodging traps, which is stressful, and it is leaving Game Pass on 2026-11-01.

9P88K6NQW12H:party.text: You and up to three friends haul furniture through physics-driven levels, throwing sofas through windows and into a van. It's the same silly, shared-chaos feel as Boomerang Fu, with a cooperative goal and simple controls anyone can pick up.
9P88K6NQW12H:party.caveat: It's capped at 4 players and co-operative, so bigger groups will have to rotate and there's no head-to-head element.

BVJLKDG2TX8H:party.text: You and friends run a kitchen together, chopping, cooking, and passing dishes while the levels shift under you. Shouting at each other over a burning stove suits a funny, chaotic couch night, and the rules are easy to explain.
BVJLKDG2TX8H:party.caveat: It's co-op only and tops out at 4 players, and it can cause real arguments if someone isn't pulling their weight.

BQRB60PW2SDL:party.text: Kart racing with split-screen for up to four, with weapons, boosts, and battle arenas. It's a quick-to-grasp, competitive game for a couch, closer in spirit to a sports game like FIFA than a puzzle or platformer.
BQRB60PW2SDL:party.caveat: It's capped at 4 and split-screen shrinks the view, and drift-boost mechanics take a few races to get comfortable with.

9NMB4T25W817:party.text: You and up to three friends wreck a sandbox town as goats, licking and headbutting things, and can try some competitive mini-games. It's physics silliness that fits the Gang Beasts crowd, with little to learn.
9NMB4T25W817:party.caveat: The sandbox has little structure, so the novelty may wear off after an hour or two and the mini-games are a small part of it.

9PMX3SK2RMG4:party.text: Each round is a different absurd dodgeball variant, so you're throwing balls at friends in short, funny matches. It joins the sports side of your tastes with party-game chaos, and up to four can play on one console.
9PMX3SK2RMG4:party.caveat: It's limited to 4 players, and since it's newer and little reviewed, I can't say how deep or varied the modes get.

C22T53SQ7FLM:party.text: A collection of 30 Rare games, including some with local multiplayer, so you can pick something short and silly for a night. It's more of a grab-bag to dip into than one dedicated party game.
C22T53SQ7FLM:party.caveat: Only a handful of the games are actually good couch multiplayer, and many are older titles with dated controls.

9PN0LC4CNLPT:party.text: A platform fighter where cartoon characters knock each other off the stage, with up to four on one console. It's close to Gang Beasts and Boomerang Fu in being a quick free-for-all, though the controls are more technical.
9PN0LC4CNLPT:party.caveat: Platform fighters reward learning each character's moves, so newcomers may get beaten by anyone who has practiced, and it's capped at 4.

9NZG72SH3H4W:party.text: You and up to three friends deliver parcels across a sandbox with floppy, ragdoll characters and unreliable vehicles. It has the wobbly physics humor of Gang Beasts, with a cooperative goal and a lot of things going wrong.
9NZG72SH3H4W:party.caveat: Critic reception is lukewarm, and the floaty controls can turn from funny to frustrating, and it's limited to 4.

9P1H8K2V0NNP:party.text: Everyone builds the racecourse together by adding obstacles and traps, then races bikes through it. That's the same build-then-sabotage loop as Ultimate Chicken Horse, and the store listing mentions local play with a larger group.
9P1H8K2V0NNP:party.caveat: The player count on one console is disputed in the data, so check that your group of 8 can all play before committing.

9NP6V9LFVJ87:party.text: A baseball game with arcade styling and a relaxed difficulty option that sits between a sports sim and something friendlier. Two can play against each other or up to four can team up on one console.
9NP6V9LFVJ87:party.caveat: Baseball is slow-paced and takes rules knowledge, so it isn't a loud chaotic party game, and the co-op cap is 4.

9P0RGJND5SR0:party.text: A faster, shorter take on Monopoly where players race around a city, buy properties, and mess with each other, with up to six on one console. It's a familiar rule set for a mixed group.
9P0RGJND5SR0:party.caveat: Steam reviews are poor at 43% positive, and it may feel more like a board game than the quick chaotic action you prefer.

C26K4DVGR45B:party.text: A colorful platformer where up to four run, jump, and slap through levels together, plus musical stages and bonus challenges. It's easy to learn and the shared-screen scramble fits Knight Squad 2 fans.
C26K4DVGR45B:party.caveat: It's mostly cooperative platforming at 4 players max, and tricky sections can frustrate less experienced friends.

9N93V5M3TG4N:party.text: A baseball game with arcade styling, local play, and up to four on one console. It covers the sports side of your tastes, with simple controls and accessible matches for a mixed group.
9N93V5M3TG4N:party.caveat: Baseball is slow-paced and rules-heavy for a chaotic party night, and it's limited to 4 players.

BP6V6QZBMFP0:party.text: Physics-driven motorbike stunts where you race through obstacle courses, with local play for up to four. The wobbly physics are funny to watch, and it mixes the competitiveness of sports with the chaos of Chicken Horse.
BP6V6QZBMFP0:party.caveat: It's tagged as difficult and the controls take practice, with mixed Steam reviews at 64%, so newcomers may get frustrated.

C3B1V55CDL0C:party.text: A free platform fighter where up to eight can brawl on one console, knocking each other off the stage with weapons and legends. It's quick to start and works for a big group like yours.
C3B1V55CDL0C:party.caveat: It has lots of characters and moves to learn, so beginners can lose badly to anyone who has played before.

9P9FTXPKQ35P:party.text: The newest in the football series you already like, with up to four players on one console. You can jump straight into matches with friends, which is a natural fit for a group that plays FIFA.
9P9FTXPKQ35P:party.caveat: It's another annual FC release, so if you already play FC 25 the local play may feel much the same, and it's limited to 4.

BVCRSR6XSDW5:party.text: Motorbike racing with physics-based stunts and tracks, with up to four competing on one console. The ragdoll crashes are funny, and it has a track editor like the build-your-own-level feel of Ultimate Chicken Horse.
BVCRSR6XSDW5:party.caveat: The tracks are tagged as difficult, and the head-to-head multiplayer is limited to 4, so it may not suit a casual crowd.

BRJNRZ9N734V:party.text: A demolition-style racing game where cars smash into each other in crashes, with a physics engine that makes every wreck different. It's a competitive, funny car-crash game that could work for a group taking turns.
BRJNRZ9N734V:party.caveat: The local player count is disputed in the data, and it's a more serious driving game, so it may not be a quick pick-up for everyone.

9PKZRN4RJRC9:party.text: Up to four gladiators are chained together and fight in an arena, using chains and surroundings to beat enemies. The forced togetherness is the kind of chaos found in Gang Beasts and Knight Squad 2, with adjustable difficulty.
9PKZRN4RJRC9:party.caveat: It's a difficult roguelike with combat-heavy runs, so it asks for more commitment than a quick party game, and it's limited to 4.

9PDGC1Z6ZHTP:party.text: A throwback to the classic arcade-style hockey game, with up to four on one console. It's easy to pick up, fast, and competitive, which fits the sports-game side of your group.
9PDGC1Z6ZHTP:party.caveat: It's deliberately retro in graphics and controls, so it may feel dated, and it's capped at 4.

9PPKR9N31BW6:party.text: A fast competitive platformer where up to four race and use items to knock each other behind. It's a chaotic, quick-round game in the same spirit as Boomerang Fu.
9PPKR9N31BW6:party.caveat: The player count is disputed in the data and little is known about its reception, and fast platforming can be hard for casual players.

C3SQQG5Q6Z64:party.text: Arcade racing with short tracks, loops, and jumps, with split-screen for up to four. It's easy to learn and each race is quick, so a group can pass the controller around.
C3SQQG5Q6Z64:party.caveat: It's about chasing perfect times and tagged as difficult, so it may feel less chaotic or funny than the games you like.

C4B8XR1LCXR5:party.text: An aerial combat game with split-screen co-op for up to four, in a pulp-adventure alternate 1930s. It's an old Xbox 360 title, so it's more of a novelty than a modern party game.
C4B8XR1LCXR5:party.caveat: It's an older game with dated controls and a flight-combat learning curve, and it's not a quick-learn party pick.

9PJGM0T0827V:party.text: An off-road racing game with four-player split-screen on gravel, ice, and sand. It has adjustable difficulty, so a mixed-skill group can race without the worst driver being left behind.
9PJGM0T0827V:party.caveat: It's a driving game rather than a chaotic one, and Steam reviews are mixed at 54%.

9NVD16NP4J8T:party.text: American football with up to four players on one console, for a group that already likes sports games like FIFA. You can play head-to-head or team up against the computer.
9NVD16NP4J8T:party.caveat: It has a lot of rules and play-calling to learn, so it's not quick for non-fans, and it's capped at 4.

9PC1KTWW5PB5:party.text: Up to four can share one console for hockey, which suits the FIFA-style sports nights. Two teams on the couch pass, shoot and check each other, with a simulation feel that rewards a bit of practice.
9PC1KTWW5PB5:party.caveat: The simulation controls are deeper than your usual quick-to-learn party picks, so newcomers may struggle at first.

9PJRQHMCFQGS:party.text: Up to four take turns rolling balls down the lane, so it works as a low-pressure couch game for groups who like sports. Everyone can follow what is happening quickly, and the competition is about score.
9PJRQHMCFQGS:party.caveat: It is a realistic bowling simulation played in turns, so it lacks the chaos and slapstick of Gang Beasts or Boomerang Fu.

C2P985H1H42H:party.text: A classic four-player minigame party game with a sci-fi setting and more than 45 minigames across six arenas. Short rounds are easy to pick up, which fits the quick, funny, competitive nights you like.
C2P985H1H42H:party.caveat: It is an old Xbox 360-era title, so visuals and minigame quality may feel dated, and it caps at four players.

9N79TQTZTQQ4:party.text: A pixel-art beat 'em up where up to four pick from 15 Marvel heroes and brawl through levels together. It is close to the co-op fighting of Minecraft Dungeons and Knight Squad 2, with easy-to-learn controls.
9N79TQTZTQQ4:party.caveat: It is co-op against enemies rather than versus chaos, and the main run is short, so it may be a one-evening game.

9PB3GGBSG27C:party.text: Up to four share a console for hockey, covering the same couch-sports ground as FIFA. Teams of friends can play against each other, and the adjustable difficulty helps mixed skill levels.
9PB3GGBSG27C:party.caveat: It is a simulation with many controls, so non-hockey fans may take a while to enjoy it.

C3553MB4P5TT:party.text: Up to four play together on one console, solving puzzles, dodging traps and fighting Egyptian underworld enemies. The teamwork and puzzle mix is similar to Lovers in a Dangerous Spacetime, with some competition over treasure.
C3553MB4P5TT:party.caveat: It leans on puzzles and has some RPG-style loot, so it is slower than the chaotic party games, and it leaves Game Pass on 2026-11-01.

9N8CD0XZKLP4:dan.text: A direct step from Ori and the Blind Forest: you platform through a large interconnected map, unlocking movement abilities that open new routes, with light environmental puzzles along the way. The combat is more fluid and the exploration loop is close to Hollow Knight's.
9N8CD0XZKLP4:dan.caveat: The story leans heavily on emotional beats, and the boss chases can be frustrating if you want slower, more deliberate platforming.

9N116V0599HB:dan.text: The direct follow-up to your all-time favorite: you play Hornet, exploring a new interconnected kingdom, fighting bosses, and finding abilities that open hidden routes. The hand-drawn look and atmosphere carry over, with faster, more acrobatic movement.
9N116V0599HB:dan.caveat: It is widely reported to be tougher than the first game, with punishing bosses and long backtracking runs that could feel grindy.

BRKMHZX1RCF2:dan.text: An Assassin's Creed set in the Caribbean, where you sail your own ship between islands, hunt, dive for wrecks, and do the usual stealth assassinations. The open exploration and sea travel fit your liking for the series.
BRKMHZX1RCF2:dan.caveat: Naval upgrades and collectibles can pad it out, and some tailing missions are more restrictive than the open-world format suggests.

9MT5NJ5W7B8Z:dan.text: You explore Hogwarts and the surrounding open world, learning spells, solving small environmental puzzles, and fighting with a spell loadout. It has a strong atmosphere and plenty of hidden things to find, similar to an Assassin's Creed map.
9MT5NJ5W7B8Z:dan.caveat: It is a large, collectible-heavy open world with fairly simple puzzles and combat, which may feel like busywork.

9N4W31HSMVVD:dan.text: A realistic medieval open-world RPG where you explore, follow quests with branching outcomes, and handle skill-based sword combat. It offers the historical immersion you get from Assassin's Creed, with more simulation detail.
9N4W31HSMVVD:dan.caveat: It is very long and slow-paced with demanding, finicky combat, which is a big time commitment.

9PDDP6ML6XHF:dan.text: You build a medieval village from scratch while hunting, gathering, crafting, and managing seasons and resources. The base building and survival loop resemble Minecraft, with some management on top.
9PDDP6ML6XHF:dan.caveat: It involves repetitive gathering and long build-up periods, which may feel grindy, and the RPG and combat parts are fairly basic.

9P4LSLG7B8CT:dan.text: A 2D metroidvania where you gain time-related powers to reach new parts of a Persian-themed map, with fast acrobatic combat and platforming. The map-driven exploration and ability gating are close to what you enjoy in Hollow Knight.
9P4LSLG7B8CT:dan.caveat: Combat is more action-oriented and flashy than Hollow Knight, and some platforming challenges are demanding.

9NLRT31Z4RWM:dan.text: You play a small fox exploring an isometric world, finding hidden paths and fighting enemies. It is built around secrets and a cryptic puzzle layer in the in-game manual, which suits your love of deep puzzles and exploration.
9NLRT31Z4RWM:dan.caveat: It gives almost no guidance, and some of the combat is quite hard, so it can feel opaque if you do not want to decipher things.

9NXQKPGMHH9G:dan.text: An older first-person RPG set in underground caverns, where you explore, solve puzzles, and cast spells by drawing runes with the mouse or controller. The puzzle and exploration focus overlaps with your tastes.
9NXQKPGMHH9G:dan.caveat: It is an early-2000s game with dated controls and interface, and it has some horror elements, which you generally avoid.

9NQGN8TGNT8P:dan.text: You hike across a ruined America delivering cargo, choosing routes, and managing terrain and weight. The traversal and quiet exploration are the core, with an atmosphere that is similar to Subnautica in being solitary.
9NQGN8TGNT8P:dan.caveat: Much of it is walking and logistics, and combat and the long, convoluted story may not appeal.

BX3JNK07Z6QK:dan.text: An open-world RPG in the Mojave where you explore, take on quests with multiple solutions, and craft ammo and items. The wasteland setting and freedom of approach suit someone who enjoys exploration.
BX3JNK07Z6QK:dan.caveat: It is rough around the edges, with dated combat and bugs, and it is long.

9NXWKGRHT31F:dan.text: A first-person open-world game on a tropical island, where you hunt, craft upgrades, take over outposts either stealthily or loudly, and explore. It is shorter than most open-world games.
9NXWKGRHT31F:dan.caveat: It is shooter-focused with violent themes, and the outpost-clearing loop is repetitive.

9PCR3Z2MSM4T:dan.text: A roguelike where you fight through procedurally arranged rooms, choosing boons and upgrades each run while the story progresses through repeated attempts. The hand-drawn art and tight combat are similar to Hollow Knight's polish.
9PCR3Z2MSM4T:dan.caveat: The run-based structure with meta-progression can feel grindy, which you tend to avoid.

C5HHPG1TXDNG:dan.text: A 3D platformer where you enter people's minds, each a themed level with its own puzzles and platforming. It has a quirky, inventive design and a story-driven structure.
C5HHPG1TXDNG:dan.caveat: It is an older game with some clunky controls and a frustrating late level.

BQ1W1T1FC14W:dan.text: A huge open-world fantasy RPG where you explore dungeons, mountains, and towns at your own pace, with plenty of atmosphere and discovery. It rewards wandering, in the spirit of Assassin's Creed exploration.
BQ1W1T1FC14W:dan.caveat: It is enormous and easy to sink hundreds of hours into, and the puzzles and combat are shallow.

9N7P8GVMF6SS:dan.text: A first-person puzzle game where you solve logic puzzles with tools like beams, boxes, and connectors across large environments, with a philosophical story. It targets the deep puzzle side of your tastes.
9N7P8GVMF6SS:dan.caveat: It is more open and story-heavy than the original, and the dialogue-heavy philosophical parts may slow the puzzle pace.

9NSFGM8J6MBJ:dan.text: You build vehicles from blocks, such as cars, boats, and aircraft, and use them to complete challenges in an open world. The engineering and tinkering have some of the same satisfaction as Infinifactory.
9NSFGM8J6MBJ:dan.caveat: The challenges are secondary to the building, and it is geared toward multiplayer, so solo play may feel thin.

9PGMNX4HG2C7:dan.text: You continue Ezio's story in Rome, assassinating targets, recruiting assassins, and rebuilding the city. It keeps the classic Assassin's Creed formula you like, with a historical setting.
9PGMNX4HG2C7:dan.caveat: The formula is familiar if you have played Assassin's Creed II, and it is mostly an expansion on it.

BW9TWC8L4JCS:dan.text: An Assassin's Creed set in ancient Greece, where you explore islands, sail, take on quests, and fight in an RPG framework. The scale of exploration and the historical setting fit your interests.
BW9TWC8L4JCS:dan.caveat: It is very long, with a lot of repetitive side content and level-based combat that can feel grindy.

9NBLGGH43KZB:dan.text: You land on planets, mine terrain with a terraforming tool, and build bases while setting up automated resource production. It combines exploration with the factory-style logistics you like in Oxygen Not Included.
9NBLGGH43KZB:dan.caveat: Progress can involve slow resource gathering, and the automation is less deep than in dedicated factory games.

BZ6W9LRPC26W:dan.text: You explore a shifting brutalist government building as a character with telekinetic powers, unlocking areas as you gain abilities in a metroidvania-style structure. The weird atmosphere is a major draw.
BZ6W9LRPC26W:dan.caveat: It is a shooter with supernatural horror touches, and the combat is a large part of it.

C5F2XDQPPJKZ:dan.text: A stealth-focused game where you approach targets in several ways, using supernatural powers and exploring detailed levels for alternate routes. It is short enough not to feel like a time sink.
C5F2XDQPPJKZ:dan.caveat: It is a standalone side entry with a smaller scope, and it assumes familiarity with earlier Dishonored games.

C3KLDKZBHNCZ:dan.text: A post-apocalyptic open-world RPG where you explore the wasteland, scavenge, and build settlements. The settlement building and survival elements overlap with Minecraft-style crafting.
C3KLDKZBHNCZ:dan.caveat: It is shooter-heavy, with repetitive settlement and scavenging loops that can become a time sink.

C0KJ40T9QD86:dan.text: A first-person open-world game in a Himalayan region, where you take outposts either stealthily or loudly, using gyrocopters and animals. It offers exploration and sandbox freedom.
C0KJ40T9QD86:dan.caveat: It is shooter-focused with a repetitive outpost loop and tends to feel similar to other Far Cry games.

BV6BRSLFJW3W:dan.text: A Far Cry set in the Stone Age, where you hunt, craft weapons, tame animals, and expand your tribe's village with no guns. The primitive survival setting is more distinctive than the usual shooter format.
BV6BRSLFJW3W:dan.caveat: It has the usual Far Cry repetitive outpost loop and resource gathering, and its story is rated weaker.

9NF5S7MLM8XT:dan.text: You explore a small open city as a cat, climbing, jumping and nudging objects around to reach new areas and trade items for progress. The gated-area exploration echoes a light metroidvania, in a short, relaxed form.
9NF5S7MLM8XT:dan.caveat: It's low-stakes and gentle, so it lacks the challenge and depth of Ori or Rain World.

9NX6K9HN4F4K:dan.text: You play an artist in a 16th-century Bavarian village, investigating murders by talking to townsfolk, piecing together clues and making choices that change later events. It's closer to a deduction-driven mystery than a puzzle game, with distinctive illuminated-manuscript art.
9NX6K9HN4F4K:dan.caveat: It's dialogue-heavy with little mechanical challenge, which may feel slow if you want hands-on puzzles.

9NBLHDB0WLHZ:dan.text: A non-violent platformer where you use a violin and precise jumping to restore a musical world. The hand-drawn look and atmosphere sit close to Ori, and the tags flag a real challenge.
9NBLHDB0WLHZ:dan.caveat: Platforming difficulty is fixed with no adjustment, and it's linear rather than a full metroidvania.

C5K89TFLSV19:dan.text: A huge open fantasy world where you pick your own direction, wander into dungeons, towns and side quests, and build a character freely. The exploration-first approach has some kinship with Assassin's Creed.
C5K89TFLSV19:dan.caveat: It's a very long, dated RPG with clunky combat, and completing it is a big time sink.

C40860J5R2MP:dan.text: A third-person survival horror game where you scavenge ammo and crafting parts, sneak around enemies and explore semi-open hub areas. Resource management and exploration are the main hooks.
C40860J5R2MP:dan.caveat: It's explicitly horror with heavy combat and gore, which you generally avoid.

9NKK6CX54183:dan.text: A classic point-and-click puzzle adventure where you control three characters across different time periods, and changes in the past alter the future. Inventory and cause-and-effect puzzles are the whole game.
9NKK6CX54183:dan.caveat: Some puzzle logic is cartoonishly obscure, so you may end up trying everything on everything.

9P8XK6X57GBF:dan.text: An action-adventure set in early 20th-century America and Japan, following a fifty-year story with open-world exploration. The historical setting may appeal to your Assassin's Creed side.
9P8XK6X57GBF:dan.caveat: It's a brawler from the Yakuza team with PvP tags, so puzzles are likely a minor part.

9P1S707BPW6W:dan.text: You play a teenager investigating her parents' disappearance, turning sketches into evidence and solving logic puzzles to uncover the mystery. It combines exploration, detective work and deduction.
9P1S707BPW6W:dan.caveat: It's new with little review data, and it's story-led, so the puzzles may be light.

9NWQ686JB33G:dan.text: You lead a mercenary band across a medieval open world, managing food, wages and gear, with turn-based tactical fights. The survival upkeep and exploration may appeal to your survival and open-world interests.
9NWQ686JB33G:dan.caveat: It's a long, grind-leaning game (about 80 hours main story), and it's leaving Game Pass soon.

C3553MB4P5TT:dan.text: An isometric action-adventure where you explore Egyptian tombs, solve environmental puzzles and dodge traps, solo or in co-op. The Tomb Raider-style puzzle-and-exploration mix is the draw.
C3553MB4P5TT:dan.caveat: Shooting is a large part of it, and reviews are mixed (68% positive), mainly because it's built for co-op.

9NRQVQ7ZRM7Z:dan.text: A story-driven action RPG in the city of Midgar, mixing real-time combat with paused tactical commands. It has a strong sci-fi setting and emotional characters.
9NRQVQ7ZRM7Z:dan.caveat: It's a long, combat-heavy, linear RPG that is only the first part of the story, with little exploration or puzzles.

9P3ZRGNQVC7D:dan.text: A short, atmospheric point-and-click adventure about a biker caught in a murder plot, with inventory puzzles and a strong soundtrack. It's a quick play with a clear story.
9P3ZRGNQVC7D:dan.caveat: Puzzles are fairly light and the game is brief, so it won't give you much deep puzzle-solving.

9P743P6195Q5:dan.text: You solve timed escape-room puzzles in a mystery-driven campus setting, alone or in co-op. It's built around reasoning through contained puzzle rooms.
9P743P6195Q5:dan.caveat: The rooms are short and timed, and the puzzles are likely gentler than Opus Magnum or Infinifactory.

9PMN4DGRT1LN:dan.text: An open-world fantasy action RPG where you fight with style-weaving combat, choose your reputation and can buy property and run shops. It's lighter and funnier than a typical serious RPG.
9PMN4DGRT1LN:dan.caveat: It's mostly combat and choices with little puzzle depth, and the data on this one is thin.

9NW6JK0ZC9J6:dan.text: A city-builder where you manage an island nation's economy, resources and politics across eras. It has the production-planning side of Oxygen Not Included but with satire.
9NW6JK0ZC9J6:dan.caveat: It's more about managing politics and budgets than designing systems, so it's less puzzle-like than your factory games.

9N6VS1BMZ3BW:dan.text: A multiplayer game where crews fly ships, fight other crews and escape with an artifact. It's mainly a sci-fi shooter.
9N6VS1BMZ3BW:dan.caveat: It's PvPvE, built around competing online, and it's leaving Game Pass soon.

9MXWL7VJ2SJW:dan.text: A survival-horror road trip where you scavenge, sneak and fight across a nightmarish 1980s America while looking for your missing parents. It has scavenging and a strong sense of place.
9MXWL7VJ2SJW:dan.caveat: It's horror with combat, which you generally avoid, and data on it is limited.

9NFW93G1GFXG:dan.text: A difficult action RPG with souls-like combat that rewards learning enemy patterns. If you like Cuphead's pattern-learning challenge, it has something similar in a different form.
9NFW93G1GFXG:dan.caveat: It's a combat-focused souls-like with no difficulty adjustment, and there's little here for puzzles or exploration.

9NL8MF491NRZ:dan.text: A 5v5 online football game with character roles and skills. It's built around team matches.
9NL8MF491NRZ:dan.caveat: It's a competitive multiplayer sports game with no overlap with your tastes.

9N40DK5N4LD4:dan.text: A turn-based RPG where you investigate murders tied to a TV world, fighting in dungeons and building bonds with friends. The mystery plot is the draw.
9N40DK5N4LD4:dan.caveat: It's a very long, dialogue-heavy JRPG with a school-life calendar, which may feel like a time sink.

9PGSDFM3JD85:dan.text: A tower-defense game where you plant defenders on a lawn grid to stop zombies. Planning plant placement and sun economy gives it a light puzzle feel.
9PGSDFM3JD85:dan.caveat: It's casual and simple, so it won't offer the depth you get from Opus Magnum or Balatro.

9P4NV23Q6QC2:online.text: You and friends play scientists trapped in a secret research facility, scavenging, crafting and building a base while fighting off anomalies. It's team-based survival with shooting, close to Deep Rock's squad feel, but at a slower, more exploratory pace.
9P4NV23Q6QC2:online.caveat: It's a long, systems-heavy survival game, so the group needs to commit to regular sessions to make progress.

9NKV34XDW014:online.text: Catch creatures, put them to work on your base and shoot your way through the open world together. Online co-op lets a group split up to gather and craft, then regroup for bosses, which is easy to play casually on a headset.
9NKV34XDW014:online.caveat: Critic reception is lukewarm, and the grind and base upkeep can feel repetitive after the first stretch.

9P7L9H478GGV:online.text: A fast, classic sci-fi shooter with co-op support, so you can fight through the Strogg campaign with a friend. The action is straightforward and the levels are short, so it works well for casual evenings.
9P7L9H478GGV:online.caveat: It's an old-school design with little hand-holding, and co-op is limited compared with Deep Rock's four-player squads.

BPKDQSSFQ9WV:online.text: A cover-based shooter built around four-player co-op through the campaign against the Locust. Dan's group can play it together on headsets with a clear objective each mission, from the studio behind Fortnite.
BPKDQSSFQ9WV:online.caveat: The campaign is short, and it's an Xbox 360-era game, so matchmaking and online population may be thin.

BXBJQ1932138:online.text: You and friends track animals across large open maps, then take careful shots. It's slow and low-pressure, with plenty of room to chat on headsets while walking and spotting.
BXBJQ1932138:online.caveat: It's very slow and has no real combat intensity, so it suits chatting more than excitement.

9NSFGM8J6MBJ:online.text: You build vehicles from parts, such as cars, boats and planes, then take them out together to explore and tackle challenges. It's a creative, low-pressure online co-op game that suits laughing about each other's builds.
9NSFGM8J6MBJ:online.caveat: There's no shooting, and the building tools take time to learn before they feel fun.

9N431PX143P8:online.text: An open-world driving game where you can cruise, explore Japan and do events with friends online. It's relaxed and easy to drop in and out of, with no ladder you have to climb.
9N431PX143P8:online.caveat: It's driving-focused, with none of the shooting or building that Dan's regular games have.

BQVQTL3PCH05:online.text: Explore planets, gather resources, craft gear and fly a ship, with co-op available so friends can join you. It mixes survival, light shooting and building at your own pace.
BQVQTL3PCH05:online.caveat: The pace is slow and solitary, and it works better as a shared hangout than as a team-action game.

9NKX70BBCDRN:online.text: An open-world racing game where you can drive around Mexico and do events with friends online. Difficulty is adjustable, and there's no pressure to compete seriously.
9NKX70BBCDRN:online.caveat: It's all driving, so it won't scratch the shooting and building itch of Dan's usual games.

BRZHFR5XBLQS:online.text: You grind rails and wall-run through a colorful city while shooting mutants with silly weapons. The tone is funny and the movement feels fast like Fortnite, with a playful, loose feel.
BRZHFR5XBLQS:online.caveat: The main campaign is mostly solo, so it may not offer much for a group on headsets.

9NQMVR9WL9FW:online.text: You crew a train that travels between strange worlds, gathering materials, crafting weapons and fighting creatures with up to four players. Building and upgrading the train together gives a squad a shared project, similar to Deep Rock's teamwork.
9NQMVR9WL9FW:online.caveat: Reception is more mixed than the other survival picks, so expect rough edges.

9PLCL2VB2SC0:online.text: A four-player co-op shooter where you hold off huge zombie hordes across story missions. It's the closest match to Deep Rock's squad-against-swarm play, with class roles and shared objectives.
9PLCL2VB2SC0:online.caveat: The campaign is short, and the missions repeat after a while.

9NKHKBQJSSC3:online.text: You fight as a robot gladiator in a voxel arena, slicing up enemies with a sword, and co-op lets a friend join. It's funny and chaotic, with more silly physics than competitive tension.
9NKHKBQJSSC3:online.caveat: The combat is melee-focused and can be hard, and co-op is less central than the solo campaign.

9P8XKV2D5DZ5:online.text: Dig for resources underground, then rush back to defend your dome from alien waves. The mining loop resembles Deep Rock's, though it's a small-scale pixel-art game.
9P8XKV2D5DZ5:online.caveat: It's mainly a solo experience, so it's less suited to a group on headsets.

9PDDP6ML6XHF:online.text: Hunt, build a village and manage seasons with co-op available, so friends can share the work of survival. It's a slow, settle-in game that rewards chatting while you craft.
9PDDP6ML6XHF:online.caveat: The pace is slow and management-heavy, with little action compared with Fortnite or Deep Rock.

9NBLGGH43KZB:online.text: You and friends explore colorful planets, mine resources and build bases, with a mining and tunneling feel similar to Deep Rock. It's relaxed, family-friendly co-op with no combat pressure.
9NBLGGH43KZB:online.caveat: There's no real combat, so those wanting action may find it too gentle.

C3QH42WRGM3R:online.text: A fast, aggressive sci-fi shooter with a single-player campaign and online multiplayer modes. It has the kind of arcade shooting that suits a quick session between other games.
C3QH42WRGM3R:online.caveat: The campaign is solo, and the multiplayer is competitive, which may feel more intense than Dan likes.

9PJ6FV3130QZ:online.text: An open-world survival game on Arrakis where you gather, craft and build bases, with co-op play and shooting. Friends can share a base and explore the desert together.
9PJ6FV3130QZ:online.caveat: It's a large, long-term online game with many systems, and some of the PvP elements may feel too intense.

9MT8PTGVHX2P:online.text: Six Halo games, with campaigns playable in online co-op, so you can fight through the story with a friend on headsets. The shooting is accessible and has a clear sense of progression.
9MT8PTGVHX2P:online.caveat: Multiplayer here can be competitive, and it's a big collection that takes time to get into.

C4DMGRPNSHXG:online.text: An open-world hacking game where you use Chicago's systems as weapons, mixing stealth and shooting. It has some online modes, but is mainly a single-player story.
C4DMGRPNSHXG:online.caveat: It's mostly a solo experience, so it adds little for Dan's regular friends-on-headsets sessions.

C0KJ40T9QD86:online.text: An open-world shooter where you take on outposts with a friend, using animals, vehicles and gyrocopters. Two-player co-op gives you a shared sandbox to mess around in.
C0KJ40T9QD86:online.caveat: Co-op is limited to two players, and the main story is better played solo.

BR7X7MVBBQKM:online.text: You liberate an open-world county with a friend in two-player co-op, using guns, vehicles and animal companions. It's chaotic, loose action that suits casual chat.
BR7X7MVBBQKM:online.caveat: Co-op is limited to two players, so a bigger group can't all join.

C1SDBNRFXT1D:online.text: A cover-based sci-fi shooter with online co-op, so Dan's group can work through the campaign together. It is straightforward, with clear objectives and a team feel, from the same studio behind Fortnite.
C1SDBNRFXT1D:online.caveat: It's an older game, with a short campaign and likely thin matchmaking.

BPRPQSKXTD1L:online.text: A real-time strategy game set in the Halo universe, with online co-op available. You build bases and command units, which is a calmer way to play with friends.
BPRPQSKXTD1L:online.caveat: It's a strategy game designed for controllers, so it's a very different style from Dan's shooters.

9PNRSC0J6DT8:online.text: You drive heavy trucks through mud and snow, winching each other out and working together to complete deliveries. It's slow, cooperative and well suited to chatting on headsets.
9PNRSC0J6DT8:online.caveat: The pace is very slow, and getting stuck repeatedly can frustrate some players.

C2N9CS4FS1QR:online.text: Four-player online co-op in a big Bolivian open world, where you plan approaches to cartel bases with friends and can go quiet or loud. Headset chatter fits well, and the pace is far less tense than a Fortnite match.
C2N9CS4FS1QR:online.caveat: It's a long, repetitive open-world campaign, so it works best if your group will stick with it for many sessions.

9PD5BM2Z8C4L:online.text: You move a character while weapons fire automatically, and you survive waves of monsters while picking upgrades. It's low-pressure and easy to play while chatting, with a similar horde-clearing feel to Deep Rock Galactic.
9PD5BM2Z8C4L:online.caveat: Co-op is local only, so playing with Dan's friends on headsets would mean something like screen sharing rather than true online play.

BSXLFN5QQZSC:online.text: A jokey hacker adventure in San Francisco where you take over cameras and drones, and can drop into co-op to cause chaos with friends. It's a relaxed, sandbox-style game that suits casual headset sessions.
BSXLFN5QQZSC:online.caveat: It's mainly a single-player story, and the co-op is a smaller side feature than the main game.

BRJNRZ9N734V:online.text: You race beaten-up cars and smash into rivals, with crashes that are often funny. It's a good pick for friends joking around on headsets, and it doesn't need the sweaty precision of serious racing.
BRJNRZ9N734V:online.caveat: Online lobbies are about racing each other rather than co-op, and it needs some driving practice to feel good.

BRKMHZX1RCF2:online.text: You sail a pirate ship around the Caribbean, board enemy vessels, and take on stealth and sword fights. It's a big sandbox with lots to explore, and it's already on your backlog.
BRKMHZX1RCF2:online.caveat: It's a single-player story with no co-op, so it won't be something to play with friends on a headset.

9N6VS1BMZ3BW:online.text: Crews pilot ships, fight other crews, and grab an artifact before escaping, mixing ship combat with first-person shooting. It's a team game that rewards talking on headsets, and the extraction goal gives you a clear objective.
9N6VS1BMZ3BW:online.caveat: It's PvPvE against other crews, which may feel more competitive than Dan likes, and it leaves Game Pass on 1 November 2026.

9NWQ686JB33G:online.text: You lead a mercenary band across a medieval open world, taking bounties, gathering resources, and fighting in turn-based battles, with online co-op available. It's slow and open-ended, which suits a group that likes to explore together.
9NWQ686JB33G:online.caveat: Turn-based combat and lots of managing supplies and gear move slowly compared with Fortnite, and it leaves Game Pass on 1 November 2026.

9PBG4MTM3JJC:online.text: One to four players drop onto alien planets, build and defend a base, then extract with what they've collected. It's the closest match here to Deep Rock Galactic's squad-based loop of mining, defending, and escaping.
9PBG4MTM3JJC:online.caveat: It's an early Game Preview, so expect missing content and rough edges.

9NL8MF491NRZ:online.text: A 5v5 online football game where players take on different roles and skills. Team play on headsets fits Dan's usual setup, and the arcade style leans toward fun over simulation.
9NL8MF491NRZ:online.caveat: It's all competitive matches against other teams, with no real co-op, so it may feel sweatier than Dan's usual play.

C3553MB4P5TT:online.text: Up to four players explore a temple together, shooting enemies, solving puzzles, and dodging traps. It's a short, easy-going co-op game that works well for a few evenings with friends on headsets.
C3553MB4P5TT:online.caveat: It's quite short, and it leaves Game Pass on 1 November 2026.

9NK039GWVTVC:online.text: A lightweight online RPG where you team up with friends to clear dungeons, defeat monsters, and collect loot to craft better gear. The low pressure and loot-driven loop suit casual co-op sessions.
9NK039GWVTVC:online.caveat: It's an early Game Preview with little track record, so content may be thin.

9P743P6195Q5:online.text: You and a friend work through escape-room puzzles in online co-op, and it needs constant talking on headsets to solve them. It's a calm change of pace from shooters.
9P743P6195Q5:online.caveat: It's all puzzle-solving with no combat, so it may not hold interest if Dan likes action more than puzzles.

9NFW93G1GFXG:online.text: A fantasy action RPG with online co-op, where you fight tough enemies alongside a friend. It's more cooperative than competitive, and it fits the combat-heavy side of your tastes.
9NFW93G1GFXG:online.caveat: Souls-like games are difficult and punishing, so it could be frustrating for a casual group.

9NS86BQ33SPX:taylor.text: A relaxed open world where you take odd jobs, try mini games and follow silly story missions at your own pace. Exploring a bright, funny sandbox is low-pressure and easy to play in short sessions.
9NS86BQ33SPX:taylor.caveat: It's a physics-based goofy sandbox, not a mystery or magic story, so the plot is light.

9NSF0BGH8D86:taylor.text: A cozy fantasy life-sim where you restore a valley, befriend Disney characters and follow gentle story quests. It suits Tay's Stardew Valley enthusiasm and is easy to play an hour at a time.
9NSF0BGH8D86:taylor.caveat: The story is sweet rather than mysterious, and the loop of gathering and crafting can feel repetitive.

BQ1W1T1FC14W:taylor.text: A huge open-world fantasy where you cast spells, explore ruins and follow quest lines at your own pace. It echoes the exploring, secrets and magic Tay liked in Hogwarts Legacy, and it's very long.
BQ1W1T1FC14W:taylor.caveat: Combat is melee-heavy and can get bloody, and the world is so large that Tay may lose track of things as in Odyssey.

9P20JCF7BV93:taylor.text: A classic turn-based fantasy quest, remastered in pixel art. You lead four heroes through towns and dungeons using magic and simple menu battles, with no frantic action.
9P20JCF7BV93:taylor.caveat: The story is very simple, with little mystery or character depth compared with Tay's usual picks.

9NWDPFPPK30V:taylor.text: A turn-based fantasy adventure where you change your party's jobs, including magic users, as you explore. Battles are calm and menu-based, and it is long enough to play an hour at a time.
9NWDPFPPK30V:taylor.caveat: The plot is basic and the difficulty can be steep, so Tay may have to retry dungeons and grind.

C2WKJJ9F5936:taylor.text: An open-world fantasy where you explore a storybook-style land, take quests and use magic alongside swordplay. It has a fairly gentle pace, and you can wander between story missions.
C2WKJJ9F5936:taylor.caveat: It's an older game, the combat is simple, and some of its darker, bloodier moments may not suit Tay.

9N8C07SS8C9D:taylor.text: A turn-based fantasy story about knights, betrayal and magic, in a pixel remaster. Menu-driven battles let Tay take their time, and the plot is more dramatic than most early RPGs.
9N8C07SS8C9D:taylor.caveat: It's an older game with a linear structure and no mystery-solving, and some battles are tough.

9N9C8SV0S16W:taylor.text: A turn-based fantasy adventure built around a flexible job system, where you mix magic and abilities across a party. It has a lighter tone and calm, menu-based combat.
9N9C8SV0S16W:taylor.caveat: The story is less serious and twisty than Tay tends to like, and the job system takes some learning.

9N255K81XBD3:taylor.text: A long, turn-based fantasy with a large cast, magic and a story that runs to dozens of hours. It suits Tay's taste for epic fantasy and playing in short sessions, with combat that isn't frantic.
9N255K81XBD3:taylor.caveat: The large cast and shifting plot may feel like too much to track, and the story has some dark turns.

9N8FQ28Z6QX3:taylor.text: A first-person adventure set in 1937, where you follow clues, solve puzzles and uncover a historical mystery across several locations. It has a strong story, exploration and adjustable difficulty.
9N8FQ28Z6QX3:taylor.caveat: It includes stealth and fistfights that can be tense, though the difficulty can be lowered.

9NZDHXL9SJJ8:taylor.text: A long, story-driven RPG where you split your time between school life and infiltrating palaces to uncover corrupt people's secrets. It has a twisty plot, humor, turn-based combat and difficulty options.
9NZDHXL9SJJ8:taylor.caveat: At 100+ hours it's a big commitment, and the story has some mature and dark themes.

9P86LLDCL5CC:taylor.text: A relaxing island life-sim where you farm, fish, craft and explore a forest at your own pace. It's close to Tay's solo Stardew Valley favorite and well suited to hour-long sessions.
9P86LLDCL5CC:taylor.caveat: It has little mystery or plot, and the amount to do can feel overwhelming, as Odyssey did.

9MZG3KH0PVZC:taylor.text: A historical adventure in Renaissance-era Constantinople, where Ezio follows a story of secrets and conspiracies. Tay enjoyed Odyssey's history and Mirage's story, and this is a more contained entry.
9MZG3KH0PVZC:taylor.caveat: It's an older game with stabbing-heavy combat and dated controls, and the tower-defense side mode is less appealing.

9NV01PJJLXN2:taylor.text: A historical adventure set in 18th-century North America, with stealth, naval travel and a story about an assassin turned hunter. It's a good fit for Tay's love of history.
9NV01PJJLXN2:taylor.caveat: Combat includes frequent violence and ship fights, and it's an older game with a darker tone.

9NH019ZFFHTV:taylor.text: A calm simulation where you diagnose problems in cars, take parts apart and put them back together like a puzzle. It has adjustable difficulty and no pressure.
9NH019ZFFHTV:taylor.caveat: It has no story or mystery, so it only appeals if Tay enjoys the mechanical puzzle-solving itself.

9NTRS771L8HL:taylor.text: A detective RPG where you investigate a murder by interrogating suspects, examining the scene and reading a lot of dialogue. It suits Tay's love of solving murders from clues, and there's no action combat.
9NTRS771L8HL:taylor.caveat: It is very text-heavy, which may be more than Tay wants, and has bleak, mature themes.

9PDC8J1BSV8B:taylor.text: A relaxed driving game where you deliver packages around a mountain town and slowly uncover its strange secrets and residents. It's short and gentle, with a hint of mystery.
9PDC8J1BSV8B:taylor.caveat: It is only about five hours, which is much shorter than the long games Tay enjoys.

9N36BLQF3FX6:taylor.text: A funny puzzle-adventure where you talk your way through quarrelling gods using dialogue as the puzzles, in a colorful mystery. It's cozy and clue-driven, with a lighthearted tone.
9N36BLQF3FX6:taylor.caveat: It's a quirky, dialogue-heavy game, so Tay may find the humor or the puzzles not to their taste.

9PKJTP6DTND3:taylor.text: A turn-based RPG mixing magic and cyberpunk, with a story-driven plot about a murder case. You talk to characters, make plans and fight in tactical battles.
9PKJTP6DTND3:taylor.caveat: The tactical combat can be tough and a bit grim, and the sci-fi setting is far from Tay's usual cozy fantasy.

BXVCFBJBNS17:taylor.text: A vast open-world fantasy where you create your own character and explore a strange land of magic at your own pace. It's long, with lots of lore, which suits Tay's patient approach.
BXVCFBJBNS17:taylor.caveat: It's an old game with dated combat and menus, and little to point you toward objectives.

9PGMNX4HG2C7:taylor.text: A historical adventure set in Renaissance Rome, with a mystery-flavored story and side activities such as rebuilding the city. It's a decent fit for Tay's history interests.
9PGMNX4HG2C7:taylor.caveat: The combat involves a lot of stabbing, and it's an older game with dated controls.

BQ9Q620NC614:taylor.text: A fairy-tale adventure with watercolor art, where a girl explores a magical world and fights in gentle turn-based battles. It's a moderate length with a story told in verse, so it's easy to follow.
BQ9Q620NC614:taylor.caveat: The story is simple, with little mystery or solving, and at about 12 hours it's shorter than Tay prefers.

9NKBDN695GTT:taylor.text: A first-person escape-room game where you search rooms, examine objects and open locks to get out. It matches Tay's love of escape-room puzzles and spotting hidden details, with no combat.
9NKBDN695GTT:taylor.caveat: It has little story, and some puzzles may be frustrating, with no difficulty options.

9NF5S7MLM8XT:taylor.text: A cozy, funny game where you play a cat exploring a city, knocking things over and meeting characters. It's a gentle open world with easy-going exploration.
9NF5S7MLM8XT:taylor.caveat: It's only a few hours long and has very little story or mystery.

9NX6K9HN4F4K:taylor.text: A historical murder mystery in 16th-century Bavaria, where you talk to villagers, collect clues and decide who to accuse. It combines Tay's interest in history and detective work, with no combat.
9NX6K9HN4F4K:taylor.caveat: There is a fair amount of reading, and the story is serious, so it's less cozy than some of Tay's other picks.

BR74RLMH966K:taylor.text: A short, gentle turn-based RPG where you trick-or-treat through a neighborhood, solve small quests and swap costumes for different battle powers. The tone is funny and cozy, and the battles are simple enough to play at a relaxed pace.
BR74RLMH966K:taylor.caveat: It is only about five or six hours and light on story depth and mystery, so it may feel slight next to Hogwarts Legacy.

9NKK6CX54183:taylor.text: A funny time-travel point-and-click where you switch between three characters across past, present and future, using inventory puzzles to fix history. It has no combat, so you can go at your own pace, and the puzzle logic is the main appeal.
9NKK6CX54183:taylor.caveat: Some puzzle solutions are famously zany and can be hard to guess, and it's a short, comedic game rather than a mystery.

9NNKJNRKFT0G:taylor.text: A fantasy action-adventure where you use magic and physics, such as fire, ice and moving objects, to climb and take down giant creatures. Magic and a story-led world fit your taste, and the play is built around experimenting with spells.
9NNKJNRKFT0G:taylor.caveat: The big creature fights are real-time and can be demanding, and there are no difficulty options, so it may be more frantic than you like.

C042M8GWKS34:taylor.text: You play a tiny stacking doll who hops into larger dolls and uses each one's special ability to solve puzzles in a charming, vintage-era world. There's no combat, and you can often find several ways to solve each puzzle.
C042M8GWKS34:taylor.caveat: It's short at around six hours and quirky rather than a deep mystery.

9P2J5D12GJL5:taylor.text: A huge open-world fantasy RPG where you can follow the main quest or wander off into guild quests, dungeons and magic. If you enjoyed exploring Hogwarts Legacy at your own pace, the long, unhurried format is similar.
9P2J5D12GJL5:taylor.caveat: It's an older game with dated visuals and clunky real-time combat, there are no difficulty options, and the world has no clear objective markers to keep track of.

BRMKDCZT0C4L:taylor.text: A light, funny action-adventure that retells all nine Star Wars films, with simple block-smashing puzzles and a lot to find in each hub world. Combat is easy-going and not gory, and you can play in short sessions.
BRMKDCZT0C4L:taylor.caveat: The puzzles are simple and there is little mystery, and the huge amount to collect may feel like the too-big-to-track problem you had with Odyssey.

9NWQ686JB33G:taylor.text: You lead a band of mercenaries across a medieval open world, taking jobs, exploring and uncovering ancient tombs. It's a very long game you can play an hour at a time, with turn-based combat that you can take at your own speed.
9NWQ686JB33G:taylor.caveat: It's a survival-style sandbox with a lot of systems to manage and little guidance, which may feel too big to keep track of, and the fights can be harsh.

9P1S707BPW6W:taylor.text: A mystery in which you play a teenager investigating her parents' disappearance, turning sketches into evidence and solving logic puzzles while exploring. It's story-led and focused on spotting clues, much like a puzzle-driven whodunit.
9P1S707BPW6W:taylor.caveat: It's a newer, little-known game, and the tone is emotional and gets darker as the case develops.

9P3ZRGNQVC7D:taylor.text: A short, funny point-and-click adventure about a biker who is drawn into a murder plot, solved through conversations and inventory puzzles. It has a strong story and a good soundtrack, and it's easy to play in short sessions.
9P3ZRGNQVC7D:taylor.caveat: It's a short, older game with some clunky action sequences and a gruff biker tone, and the mystery is thin compared with a proper whodunit.

9PMN4DGRT1LN:taylor.text: A fairytale-style open-world action RPG with humor, magic, spell and sword combat, and a village you can shop and settle in. Its storybook fantasy tone is close to what you enjoyed in Hogwarts Legacy.
9PMN4DGRT1LN:taylor.caveat: Combat is real-time and there are no difficulty options, and the story seems to lean on choices more than on mystery.

9NRQVQ7ZRM7Z:taylor.text: A story-heavy fantasy sci-fi RPG with a big cast and magic, set in a sprawling city. The story is the main draw, and a lot of the 40 hours is spent on conversations and exploring.
9NRQVQ7ZRM7Z:taylor.caveat: The combat is fast and constant, and you've said you don't want frantic fights, so it may be a poor fit.

9N40DK5N4LD4:taylor.text: A turn-based RPG with a murder mystery at its core: you investigate strange deaths in a small town, with a team of friends and a long story. Turn-based fights suit a non-frantic pace.
9N40DK5N4LD4:taylor.caveat: The story is dark in places and has some supernatural horror, and time-management and social systems add a lot to keep track of.

9P743P6195Q5:taylor.text: A set of escape-room puzzle rooms with an overarching conspiracy to unravel, which you can play alone. It fits your liking for locks and for spotting hidden details.
9P743P6195Q5:taylor.caveat: The story is a light framework for the rooms, and it's a newer game with few details yet, so it may not satisfy a craving for a deep mystery.

C3553MB4P5TT:taylor.text: An Egyptian-themed adventure with tomb puzzles and traps, and Lara Croft exploring a temple. The puzzles and the setting suit your interest in history and secrets.
C3553MB4P5TT:taylor.caveat: It's a shooter with hordes of enemies and constant combat, and it's built for co-op, so it will probably feel too frantic for you.
